key_insight: Fine-tuning large language models with a dual-head architecture yields jointly calibrated probability estimates and fluent verbalized explanations, enabling reliable, explainable decisions from a single model.
problem_solved: LLMs can generate natural explanations but lack reliable, quantitative probabilities for decision-making; the paper addresses how to produce both well-calibrated probabilities and coherent explanations from one fine-tuned model.
method: Dual-head fine-tuning: one head outputs a probabilistic classification distribution, the other generates a verbalized explanation.
Joint training objective that combines classification loss (with calibration-aware terms) and generative/explanation loss, aligning probability mass with explanation content.

Evaluation and calibration techniques (e.g., reliability/expected calibration error monitoring and dataset-specific explanation supervision) to improve and validate both uncertainty and explanation fidelity.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical way to deploy LLMs as decision-support tools that report trustworthy uncertainty and human-readable rationales, improving transparency and risk-aware automation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing shared encoder with two heads (classification probabilities + explanation generator)
Reliability diagram (calibration curve) comparing baseline LLM vs CLSGen (ECE reduction)
Example pipeline card: input → probabilistic output (histogram/confidence) + generated explanation text for the same sample
Metric bar chart summarizing accuracy, ECE, and explanation quality/fidelity scores
paper_title: CLSGen: A Dual-Head Fine-Tuning Framework for Joint Probabilistic Classification and Verbalized Explanation
paper_authors: WonJin Yoon, Kangyu Zhu, Ian Bulovic, Autumn Sehy, Yanjun Gao
